output.content:
Sports cancellations jumped after the Big Game, led by playback problems, event-only churn and payment failures.

Sports recorded 15,800 cancellations versus 8,977 expected. Of the 6,823 excess cancellations, playback problems accounted for 2,302, or 33.7%; event-only churn accounted for 2,064, or 30.3%; payment failures accounted for 1,999, or 29.3%; and 458, or 6.7%, remained unexplained. The “Payment retry policy” says declined sign-ups receive one retry after 1 hour and have a 24-hour grace window, but processor_timeout declines were not retried and instead cancelled when that window expired. 965 Sports support conversations said they were charged, declined and cancelled. The subscriber count of 15,800 reconciled within tolerance to the Finance ledger’s 15,760, a difference of 40.

drivers.label: Couldn't watch the halftime show properly
drivers.evidence: Voluntary cancels by viewers with 5+ minutes of buffering in the alerted cell that night (silver_sessions, gold_anomaly_alerts)

drivers.label: Sign-up payment timed out and was never retried
drivers.evidence: Involuntary cancels after a processor_timeout sign-up decline with no retry and an expired 24 h grace window (fact_billing_attempts); wins any overlap with playback

drivers.label: Expected event-only cancels
drivers.evidence: event_promo sign-ups cancelling within 24 h: 2.9% on this night vs 2.8% and 2.9% on the prior big-game nights

drivers.label: Not explained yet
drivers.evidence: Cancels above the baseline that match none of the rules above
